question: What is the principal layout difference between the pathway grade crossing and the sidewalk grade crossing in Figure 8E-1?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The principal difference is one of right-of-way and relationship to the roadway. In panel A of Figure 8E-1, the pathway crosses the tracks within its own independent pathway right-of-way, separated from any roadway; in panel B, the sidewalk runs parallel to and immediately adjacent to a roadway within the highway right-of-way, so it crosses the tracks alongside the roadway. Because the sidewalk is close to the roadway's traveled way, the roadway crossing's traffic control devices can influence sidewalk users, whereas they cannot adequately warn users of a separated pathway. Standards (mandatory): - "Detectable warnings (see Chapter 3C) shall be used at pathway grade crossings where pedestrian travel is permitted and at sidewalk grade crossings and shall extend across the full width of the pathway or sidewalk." (Both panels of Figure 8E-1 show detectable warnings on each approach.) Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 8E-1 shows panel A with a pathway in its own labeled "Pathway right-of-way" crossing the railroad independently of any roadway, and panel B with a sidewalk running beside a roadway within the labeled "Highway right-of-way," both with detectable warnings on each side of the tracks within the railroad right-of-way. [Image 5] and [Image 7] show the full-page context of Figure 8E-1 and the accompanying Section 8E.01 Support text explaining that a pathway is frequently placed in its own right-of-way independent of any roadway, while a sidewalk runs parallel to a roadway within the highway right-of-way. Citations: - Section 8E.01 Support §4 (p.1035) - Section 8E.02 Support §4 (p.1036) - Section 8E.04 Standard §7 (p.1038) - Figure 8E-1 (p.1035) - Page 1076 - Page 1077
gold_answer: The pathway crossing is on a separate pathway alignment outside the roadway, whereas the sidewalk crossing is part of the highway corridor alongside the roadway and crosses the tracks with the roadway.
